text: dsh-intelligent-ui 是面向 DSH 网页客户端的生成式界面插件。它注册 artifact 工具和界面组件，让模型把交互页面写成 DIL 声明式文档，编译后在会话中呈现；也可用 HTML 文档作为另一种渲染路径。用户可以创建计算器、图表或其他可操作界面，修改既有产物并保留版本，还能在右侧产物面板中再次打开。产物会保存在本地，供应用重启后继续读取和修改。安装后无需额外账号或 API 密钥。

dsh-intelligent-ui lets DSH generate interactive interfaces from DIL documents, with an HTML option. Users can revise artifacts, retain versions, and reopen them in a sidebar. Artifacts persist locally across restarts; no extra account or API key is required.
想让 DSH 直接生成可以操作的计算器或图表。
能不能在对话里生成一个带滑块和开关的页面？
我想让模型做出的界面可以在回答里直接显示。
如何让生成的页面修改后保留我刚才输入的状态？
想把之前做过的交互页面保存下来，下次继续修改。
给 DSH 加一个能长期查看本会话生成内容的侧栏。
I want the assistant to make an interactive calculator instead of describing one.
Can generated interfaces stay available and editable after restarting the app?
dsh-intelligent-ui 的功能「DIL 交互界面」：模型可通过 artifact 工具提交 DIL 文档，插件将其编译成可操作的界面，并在回复中的 artifact 标记位置显示。
dsh-intelligent-ui 的功能「HTML 文档渲染」：创建时可选择 html 引擎并提供 CSS 与 HTML，插件将自包含文档作为产物呈现，供组件清单无法表达的界面使用。
dsh-intelligent-ui 的功能「原地修改与版本」：对已有产物执行 patch 时以精确文本替换生成新版本；存储层保留版本记录，使旧版本仍可读取。
dsh-intelligent-ui 的功能「本地持久化」：产物存储在本地目录，记录版本内容和索引；默认目录位于用户主目录下的 DSH storage。
dsh-intelligent-ui 的功能「右侧产物面板」：插件注册会话产物的右侧面板，可选择产物并查看实时预览；从对话中的产物视图也可打开侧栏。

**Generative UI for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): the model writes an interface instead of describing one.**

dsh-intelligent-ui README · dsh-intelligent-ui：An open-source take on what ChatGPT calls **Intelligent UI** (internal codename *DIL*) and Claude calls **Artifacts** — the model's answer stops being prose about a dashboard and becomes the dashboard. Sliders you can drag, toggles you can flip, numbers that recompute locally with no second model call, and a card the model can revise in place while keeping your place.

Everything is one tool (`artifact`), two rendering paths, and an on-disk artifact layer.

dsh-intelligent-ui README · dsh-intelligent-ui：> Keywords: DSH plugin · DeepSeek Harness plugin · generative UI · GenUI · ChatGPT Intelligent UI · Claude Artifacts · declarative DSL · worker sandbox · native DOM render tree · artifact version history

dsh-intelligent-ui README · What it is：Ask for something you would otherwise only read about — *"a plan calculator where I can change seats and billing period"* — and the reply **is** a working calculator. The model writes a small declarative document, DSH compiles and runs it in a sandbox, and the host draws the result with native DOM: real controls, the host's own type scale, the host's own colours, correct in both light and dark mode.

Three things follow from that, and they are the whole point:

dsh-intelligent-ui README · What it is：- **You operate the answer.** A chart whose inputs you change, a checklist you tick, a config you tune — not a screenshot of one.
- **It stays correct.** Ask for a change and the model patches the same artifact in place. Version history means the revision you were looking at is still on disk.
- **It survives the session.** Artifacts are persisted, so a card from last week is still patched in place today, after an app restart.

dsh-intelligent-ui README · The two paths：| | Compiled path — `engine: "dil"` (default) | Escape hatch — `engine: "html"` |
|---|---|---|
| The model writes | a DIL document: prose, `{@body …}` declarations, one root `<box>` | a self-contained document: `css`, then `html` |
| Who executes it | a **DOM-less Worker** inside the frame runs the compiled program | the frame runs the document itself |
| Who draws it | **the host**, from a render tree, using native DOM | the frame draws itself |
| What you get | theme for free, few tokens on the wire, controls wired to each other, structure streams out first | no ceiling (canvas, WebGL, D3, your own simulation) |

dsh-intelligent-ui README · The two paths：The distinction that matters: **the sandbox is an execution container, not a display container.** Compiled code runs in a Worker that has no DOM, and emits a render tree the host draws. "Code inside the card reaching the host's elements" is therefore not blocked — there is no path for it to happen.

dsh-intelligent-ui README · Install：From npm:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-intelligent-ui
```

For the Electron **desktop** profile, use the app's Plugin Manager instead; the CLI refuses that profile.

Or straight from the repository:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:yunyv/dsh-intelligent-ui
```

Requires DSH **>= 0.2.1-rc.1** (`engines.dsh`). Then **restart the app**. The build output is committed, so a git install needs no build step and no build permission.

dsh-intelligent-ui README · Install：From a tarball, if you prefer to pin an exact artifact:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add ./dsh-intelligent-ui-0.1.1.tgz
```

From a checkout, for development:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/yunyv/dsh-intelligent-ui && cd dsh-intelligent-ui
pnpm install && pnpm run check
bash scripts/reinstall-desktop.sh
```

dsh-intelligent-ui README · Install：Do not install this by linking the source directory. A link exposes `node_modules/@deepseek-ai/*` — which exists only for type checking — to the Loader; Node resolves to those copies, their own transitive peers are not installed, and the import throws `Cannot find package`, which takes the whole plugin down.

dsh-intelligent-ui README · Use：The authoring contract — the full component inventory, the rules that make a document run — ships as a bundled **skill**, so it loads only when a turn is actually about to write one rather than sitting in every request. Say `skill genui` to read it.

Where the card appears is under the model's control too: it writes a fenced block whose language is `dsh-artifact` and whose only content is the artifact id, and the frame is mounted at that point in the answer.

dsh-intelligent-ui README · How it works：```
src/tool.ts            every decision the tool makes; imports no @deepseek-ai/*, so tests drive it directly
src/index.ts           the harness binding: Config, store root, registration, presentation hooks
src/dil/               the ported streaming DIL compiler (parser, codegen, streaming boundaries, fallback)
src/store/             the on-disk artifact layer

dsh-intelligent-ui README · How it works：The compiler is a streaming compiler. It is fed a growing prefix of the document and reports which components have closed and which are still open, so the card can appear while the model is still typing it. Recovery is not all-or-nothing: a half-written element is dropped and everything around it still renders.

An artifact can be on screen twice — live in its card and again in the right column — and the two share one state, so a control moved in either one moves both.

dsh-intelligent-ui README · The artifact store：Persisted under `~/.dsh/storages/dsh-intelligent-ui/`, with the data model borrowed from [coda0HQ/open-artifacts](https://github.com/coda0HQ/open-artifacts) (MIT):

```text
index.json                               the catalogue; never holds content
artifacts/art-xxxxxxxx/versions/
  v0001.html  v0001.json                 content and metadata kept apart
  v0002.html  v0002.json

dsh-intelligent-ui README · The artifact store：Versions are **appended, never rewritten**. Each carries `versionNumber`, `parentVersionId`, `contentSha256`, `contentBytes` and a `changelog`; `restore` appends a new head rather than editing history; `expectedLatestVersion` gives optimistic concurrency; `read(id, N)` fetches any historical revision.

dsh-intelligent-ui README · The artifact store：The write order is content → sidecar → atomic index replace, and both the read and the write path treat the disk as the source of truth, so a crash in the middle cannot leave the head pointing at bytes that are not there.

dsh-intelligent-ui README · Configuration：| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `storeRoot` | `''` | artifact directory; empty means `~/.dsh/storages/dsh-intelligent-ui` |
| `maxSourceBytes` | `2000000` | refuse a document larger than this |
| `maxArtifactsPerSession` | `40` | per-session artifact ceiling |
| `includeDegradedText` | `true` | append the plain-text projection the model can read back |

dsh-intelligent-ui README · Development：```sh
pnpm run check     # typecheck (3 projects) && build && vitest && the vendored upstream suite
```

442 tests pass: 344 ours, 98 vendored from upstream. The browser half is tested against the **built** `lib/client.js` through the real `__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory })` contract, so a registration or render failure there is a real defect rather than a test-harness artefact.

dsh-intelligent-ui README · Development：To iterate on `src/client/**` without restarting the app, build and copy the bundle into the installed copy; the browser picks it up:

```sh
pnpm run build && cp lib/client.js ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules/dsh-intelligent-ui/lib/client.js
```

Anything on the host side needs a reinstall **and a restart**.
dsh-intelligent-ui README · Notes for plugin authors：Three failures worth knowing about, all of which are invisible in review and were found the hard way.

dsh-intelligent-ui README · Notes for plugin authors：**A host half fails silently.** An unresolvable module specifier leaves no trace in the transcript: the plugin entry simply reports `fiberPhase: failed` and its tool is absent. Declaring a package in `peerDependencies` to get its types makes the bundler externalise it — so if the runtime does not actually ship that package, the plugin never runs while every `inject`, Config and skill assertion still passes. `tests/host-bundle.spec.ts` asserts that the built entry imports nothing outside the runtime-provided set.

dsh-intelligent-ui README · Notes for plugin authors：**A successfully-loaded module is cached for the life of the process.** Toggling a plugin entry off and on re-imports it, which rescues a load that *failed*. It does not re-read a file whose module already loaded: the ESM cache answers, `apply` runs against the old code, and the package on disk is irrelevant. Changed code needs a restart.

dsh-intelligent-ui README · Notes for plugin authors：**`ctx.inject(deps, cb)` is how you wait for an optional service.** Probing with `ctx.get(name)` and returning when it is absent works right up until a cold start runs your plugin before the provider is up, and then it fails intermittently forever. An optional dependency is not a hard `inject` entry, and it is not a one-shot probe — it is something to wait for.

dsh-intelligent-ui README · Notes for plugin authors：> **On the name.** This was called `dsh-genui` until it was clear that name was taken: [lhuans/dsh-genui](https://github.com/lhuans/dsh-genui) is an unrelated DSH generative-UI plugin that got there first, and a generic name said nothing about the approach here. The two differ where it counts — that one renders Vue components from a schema, this one compiles a declarative document and hands the host a render tree.

dsh-intelligent-ui README · Provenance and license：MIT. The DIL path vendors [Disdjj/intelligent-ui-demo](https://github.com/Disdjj/intelligent-ui-demo) (MIT) verbatim under `vendor/`; the compiler and sandbox under `src/dil/` and `src/client/dil/` are ports of it. Exact commits, what was changed and why are in [PROVENANCE.md](PROVENANCE.md). Third-party code is never edited in place — changes happen in `src/`.

dsh-intelligent-ui README · Provenance and license：The protocol is a snapshot of ChatGPT's DIL `protocolVersion 14` and upstream may change it at any time; the details are sealed inside `src/dil/` and `src/client/dil/`.

Two deliberate divergences from upstream, both recorded as tests rather than as drift: a closing tag inside a block no longer swallows the rest of the document, and the plain-text projection keeps an interpolation's place (`n = {n}` rather than `n = `) so a terminal reader does not get a sentence with a hole in it.
